record.paper_title: Some open questions on morphological operators and representations in the deep learning era: A personal vision
record.original_question: For hybrid networks that include morphological layers, is there an efficient learning technique that combines optimization inspired by tropical geometry with stochastic gradient descent, what gradient-descent optimizers work best, and can alternating optimization between convolution layers and morphological layers improve training?

evidence.quote: Is there any efficient network learning technique which can combine the optimization techniques inspired from tropical geometry and stochastic gradient descent? What are the best gradient-descent optimizers in the case of hybrid networks including morphological layers? Is there any strategy of alternate optimization between the convolution layers and the morphological layers?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider hybrid feed-forward neural networks whose layers include both classical linear/convolutional layers and morphological layers. A morphological layer is one whose neurons compute operations in the (max,+) or (min,+) semiring; concretely, a typical morphological neuron implements a dilation of the form y = max_{i}(x_i + w_i) or an erosion y = min_{i}(x_i + w_i), where w_i are trainable parameters. Such layers are naturally described in tropical algebra/tropical geometry: the function realized by a morphological (or piecewise-linear) network can be written as a tropical polynomial, and learning can in principle be formulated using tools from tropical geometry (e.g., difference-of-convex programming on max-plus expressions, Newton polytope approximations).

Address the following questions for the training of such hybrid networks:

(a) Construct an efficient training scheme that combines optimization techniques inspired by tropical geometry (for the morphological layers) with stochastic gradient descent (for the remaining layers), and analyze its convergence and empirical performance.

(b) Among standard gradient-descent–based optimizers (e.g., vanilla SGD, SGD with momentum/Nesterov, Adam, RMSProp, AdaGrad, AdamW), identify which optimizer(s) are best suited to training hybrid networks containing morphological layers, and justify the choice.

(c) Determine whether an alternating optimization strategy — in which the parameters of the convolutional/linear layers and those of the morphological layers are updated in alternation rather than jointly — improves training (in terms of convergence speed, stability, or final accuracy) compared with joint optimization of all parameters.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has addressed parts of these questions. Dimitriadis and Maragos (2021) and follow-ups formulate morphological-classifier training as a Difference-of-Convex (tropical-geometry-motivated) problem and study gradient-descent variants, reporting empirical optimizer choices (e.g., Adam at η≈1e-3, SGD at η≈0.09; or Adam-then-SGD-with-Nesterov schedules for hybrid linear-morphological nets, as in Sparse Hybrid Linear-Morphological Networks, 2025). However, no definitive answer establishes a uniformly best optimizer or a fully validated alternating scheme; the broader open questions about combining tropical-geometry optimization with SGD and about alternating layer-wise training remain only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Advances in the training, pruning and enforcement of shape constraints of Morphological Neural Networks using Tropical Algebra
status_evidence.snippet: Training of binary morphological classifiers is formulated as a Difference-of-Convex optimization problem and extended to multiclass tasks; gradient descent variants are studied.
status_evidence.claim: Tropical-algebra-based DC optimization combined with gradient-descent variants has been developed for morphological networks.

status_evidence.title: Sparse Hybrid Linear-Morphological Networks
status_evidence.snippet: Hybrid linear-morphological networks trained with Adam (lr 1e-4) for initial epochs followed by SGD with Nesterov momentum (0.9, lr 1e-3).
status_evidence.claim: Recent empirical work proposes specific optimizer schedules for hybrid linear-morphological networks, partially addressing the optimizer-choice question.

status_evidence.title: Hybrid Training of Morphological Neural Networks: A Comparative Study
status_evidence.snippet: Comparative study of hybrid training procedures for morphological neural networks.
status_evidence.claim: Earlier hybrid training procedures exist but do not give a definitive best-strategy answer.
